coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 5–6 miles, Z2 (140–150 bpm max), rolling terrain if available but nothing steep. You're 3 days out from a 50K with 2,500m vert; your resting HR is 52 and recovery score is maxed—your nervous system is primed. This is a sharpener, not a builder. Keep it conversational, no tempo work, no repeats. Finish feeling like you could do another 3 miles, not like you nailed anything.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You're sleeping 10.7 hours and running easy volume; don't overfuel in a false carb-load panic. Eat normally at breakfast and lunch (aim for 4–5g carb/kg bodyweight across the day), then a light dinner. Tomorrow and Thursday you'll push carbs up slightly (6–7g/kg), but today is maintenance. Hydration stays consistent—no need to superharge now. Focus on getting sodium and electrolytes in consistent small doses to train your gut for the alpine aid station reality.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Your sleep is exceptional (10.73h, 87.3% efficiency) and resting HR is the lowest in your 30-day average—you're ready. Maintain that sleep window tonight; don't stay up late from pre-race nerves. Ice baths, compression, or aggressive massage are counterproductive now—risk disrupting the nervous system calibration you've built. 20–30 minute easy walk this evening if restless, otherwise rest and hydrate.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You've done the work over 34 weeks. The 50K demands patience on the uphills and controlled descent technique on the downs—neither of which changes in the next 72 hours. Spend tonight reviewing the course profile (know which climbs are runnable vs. hike-able) and your aid station nutrition plan. Run your easy 5–6 miles tomorrow with zero pressure; let the taper anxiety pass through you, not into you.
